subproblem.title: Borel measurability of the upper/lower n-densities and their level sets (Simon Ch. 1, 3.2; parent step 8)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and μ an s-finite Borel measure on ℝ^N. Then x ↦ limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) and x ↦ liminf_{ρ↓0} μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) are Borel functions ℝ^N → [0,∞], and for every c ∈ [0,∞] the set {x : Θ^n(μ,x) exists and equals c} is a Borel set.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) [SFinite μ], Measurable (fun x ↦ limsup (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ Measurable (fun x ↦ liminf (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, MeasurableSet {x | HasDensity n μ x c}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Borel-measurability ingredient of step 8 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 1, 3.2: the upper and lower densities are Borel functions), for an s-finite measure (no local finiteness, so it applies to μ_V, which may give infinite mass to balls meeting ∂U). Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞); B̄_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ; d(x,ρ) := densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n); D⁺(x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} d(x,ρ), D⁻(x) := liminf_{ρ↓0} d(x,ρ) (filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ).

1. Fixed radius. For ρ ∈ ℝ, x ↦ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) is Borel: the set C_ρ := {(x,y) ∈ ℝ^N × ℝ^N : dist(y,x) ≤ ρ} is closed, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra (which is the Borel σ-algebra, ℝ^N being second countable: Prod.borelSpace), and its section {y : (x,y) ∈ C_ρ} is B̄_ρ(x); for s-finite μ, x ↦ μ({y : (x,y) ∈ C}) is measurable for every measurable C (measurable_measure_prodMk_left). Dividing by the constant ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n, x ↦ d(x,ρ) is Borel.

2. Rational radii. Fix x and δ > 0; write φ(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(x)) (nondecreasing in ρ), ψ(ρ) := ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n (continuous on (0,∞) with values in (0,∞)), so d(x,ρ) = φ(ρ)/ψ(ρ).
 (a) sup_{ρ∈(0,δ)} d(x,ρ) = sup_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q). "≥" is clear. For "≤" let ρ ∈ (0,δ). If φ(ρ) = ∞ then φ(q) = ∞ = d(x,q) for every rational q ∈ (ρ,δ), and such q exist. Otherwise, for rational q ∈ (ρ,δ), d(x,q) = φ(q)/ψ(q) ≥ φ(ρ)/ψ(q), and φ(ρ)/ψ(q) → φ(ρ)/ψ(ρ) = d(x,ρ) as q ↓ ρ through rationals (ψ continuous and positive at ρ, φ(ρ) finite); hence d(x,ρ) ≤ sup_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q).
 (b) inf_{ρ∈(0,δ)} d(x,ρ) = inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q). "≤" is clear. For "≥" let ρ ∈ (0,δ); if φ(ρ) = ∞ then d(x,ρ) = ∞ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, for rational q ∈ (0,ρ), d(x,q) = φ(q)/ψ(q) ≤ φ(ρ)/ψ(q) → d(x,ρ) as q ↑ ρ through rationals, so inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q) ≤ d(x,ρ).

3. Borel densities (first two conjuncts). The intervals (0, 1/(m+1)), m ∈ ℕ, form a basis of 𝓝[>]0, so by Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup / liminf_eq_iSup_iInf and step 2, D⁺(x) = inf_m sup_{q∈ℚ∩(0,1/(m+1))} d(x,q) and D⁻(x) = sup_m inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,1/(m+1))} d(x,q). These are countable infima/suprema of the Borel functions x ↦ d(x,q) of step 1, hence D⁺ and D⁻ are Borel.

4. Level sets (third conjunct). [0,∞] is a complete linear order with the order topology and 𝓝[>]0 is a nontrivial filter, so d(x,·) → c along 𝓝[>]0 iff D⁻(x) = c and D⁺(x) = c (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq, Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq, tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup). Hence {x : HasDensity n μ x c} = D⁺⁻¹({c}) ∩ D⁻⁻¹({c}), the intersection of preimages of the closed (Borel) singleton {c} under Borel maps; it is Borel. ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) is Borel for s-finite μ (measurable_measure_prodMk_left on the closed set {dist ≤ ρ}).
Monotonicity of ρ ↦ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and continuity of ω_nρ^n reduce sup/inf over real radii in (0,δ) to rational radii.
limsup and liminf along 𝓝[>]0 are countable inf-sup / sup-inf of Borel functions, hence Borel.
HasDensity n μ x c ⟺ limsup = c ∧ liminf = c, so the level set is Borel.

subproblem.title: σ-finiteness of μ⌞M for a positive locally integrable multiplicity (parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^N, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, M ⊆ U, and θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M and θ μ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U. Then the restriction μ⌞M (Mathlib μ.restrict M, so (μ⌞M)(B) = μ(B ∩ M) for Borel B; M need not be measurable) is σ-finite.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (U M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μ) → SigmaFinite (μ.restrict M)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the multiplicity θ of v(M,θ) is positive on M and locally integrable, Simon Ch. 8 p. 206 / Remark 5.9), stated for an arbitrary measure μ on ℝ^N = Euclidean N; the parent applies it with μ = H^n = μHE[n]. Notation: μ⌞E := μ.restrict E; B̄_q(c) := closedBall c q.

1. Restrictions to arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) sets E: (i) (μ⌞E)(B) = μ(B ∩ E) for every Borel B (Measure.restrict_apply); (ii) μ(t ∩ E) ≤ (μ⌞E)(t) for every set t (Measure.le_restrict_apply).

2. Countable compact cover of U. ℝ^N is separable; fix a countable dense D ⊆ ℝ^N (TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). Let 𝒦 be the countable family of closed balls B̄_q(c) with c ∈ D, q ∈ ℚ, q > 0 and B̄_q(c) ⊆ U. Each K ∈ 𝒦 is compact (ℝ^N is proper) and K ⊆ U. Moreover U = ⋃𝒦: for y ∈ U choose ε > 0 with B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U (U open), a rational q with 0 < q < ε/2 and c ∈ D with |c − y| < q; then y ∈ B̄_q(c) ⊆ B̄_{2q}(y) ⊆ B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U, so B̄_q(c) ∈ 𝒦.

3. Borel representatives. Fix K ∈ 𝒦 and put μ_K := μ⌞(M ∩ K). By hypothesis θ is μ_K-integrable, hence μ_K-a.e. strongly measurable: there is a Borel g_K : ℝ^N → ℝ with μ_K(E_K) = 0, where E_K := {y : θ(y) ≠ g_K(y)}. Since the integrands agree μ_K-a.e., ∫⁻ ofReal(g_K) dμ_K = ∫⁻ ofReal(θ) dμ_K < ∞ (Integrable.lintegral_lt_top).

4. A countable Borel cover of ℝ^N. Let 𝒮 consist of the closed set Uᶜ, the sets Z_K := K ∩ {g_K ≤ 0} (K ∈ 𝒦) and S_{K,k} := K ∩ {g_K ≥ 1/(k+1)} (K ∈ 𝒦, k ∈ ℕ). 𝒮 is countable and ⋃𝒮 = ℝ^N: a point y ∉ U lies in Uᶜ; a point y ∈ U lies in some K ∈ 𝒦 (step 2), and then either g_K(y) ≤ 0 (so y ∈ Z_K) or g_K(y) > 0, whence g_K(y) ≥ 1/(k+1) for some k ∈ ℕ (so y ∈ S_{K,k}).

5. Each member of 𝒮 has finite μ⌞M-measure.
 (a) (μ⌞M)(Uᶜ) = μ(Uᶜ ∩ M) = μ(∅) = 0, because M ⊆ U.
 (b) (μ⌞M)(Z_K) = μ(Z_K ∩ M) by 1(i). If y ∈ Z_K ∩ M then θ(y) > 0 ≥ g_K(y), so y ∈ E_K ∩ (M ∩ K). By 1(ii) and step 3, μ(Z_K ∩ M) ≤ μ(E_K ∩ (M ∩ K)) ≤ μ_K(E_K) = 0.
 (c) Let c_k := 1/(k+1) > 0 and L_k := {y : g_K(y) ≥ c_k}, a Borel set. By 1(i), (μ⌞M)(S_{K,k}) = μ(K ∩ L_k ∩ M) = μ(L_k ∩ (M ∩ K)) = μ_K(L_k). Since c_k > 0, L_k = {y : ofReal(c_k) ≤ ofReal(g_K(y))}, so Markov's inequality for the measurable function ofReal∘g_K (mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀) gives ofReal(c_k)·μ_K(L_k) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(g_K) dμ_K < ∞, i.e. (μ⌞M)(S_{K,k}) ≤ (k+1)·∫⁻ ofReal(θ) dμ_K < ∞.

6. Since ℝ^N is covered by the countably many sets in 𝒮, each of finite μ⌞M-measure, μ⌞M is σ-finite (Measure.sigmaFinite_of_countable). ∎
proof_key_steps: Restriction facts for arbitrary sets: (μ⌞E)(B) = μ(B∩E) for Borel B and μ(t∩E) ≤ (μ⌞E)(t).
U is the union of the countable family 𝒦 of closed balls with dense-set centres and rational radii contained in U.
For K ∈ 𝒦 pick a Borel g_K equal to θ μ⌞(M∩K)-a.e., with ∫⁻ ofReal g_K d(μ⌞(M∩K)) < ∞.
Uᶜ, Z_K = K ∩ {g_K ≤ 0} and S_{K,k} = K ∩ {g_K ≥ 1/(k+1)} form a countable cover of ℝ^N.
(μ⌞M)(Uᶜ) = 0 since M ⊆ U; (μ⌞M)(Z_K) = 0 since θ > 0 on M; (μ⌞M)(S_{K,k}) < ∞ by Markov.
Measure.sigmaFinite_of_countable gives σ-finiteness of μ⌞M.

subproblem.title: Density of θH^n⌞M at a weighted approximate tangent point (Simon Ch. 3 Remark 1.8(2); parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^N H^n-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ ≥ 0 on M, x ∈ M, r₀ > 0 with θ H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x), and P ⊆ ℝ^N a linear subspace such that M has weighted approximate tangent space P at x with respect to θ (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7: dim P = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x+ry) dH^n(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N,ℝ), η_{x,r}(z) = r^{-1}(z−x)). Then the measure ν := (H^n⌞M) with density ofReal∘θ (so ν(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal θ dH^n for Borel B) has n-dimensional density θ(x) at x: ν(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)) (r₀ : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 ≤ θ y) → x ∈ M → 0 < r₀ → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall x r₀) μHE[n] → Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P → HasDensity n (((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M).withDensity fun y ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ y)) x (ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N; ω_n := unitBallVolume n, a number in (0,∞) (the volume of the unit ball of ℝ^n; ω_0 = 1), also used for its real value; B̄_s(z) := closedBall z s; η_r := Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, η_r(z) = r^{-1}(z − x); ν := (H^n⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ). For Borel B, ν(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫⁻_M 1_B(z) ofReal θ(z) dH^n(z) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). The hypothesis HWATS(n,M,θ,x,P) says: finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N,ℝ), ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH^n(y) → θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n as r ↓ 0. Since x ∈ M, θ(x) ≥ 0.

1. Change of variables. For r > 0 and every set A ⊆ ℝ^N, H^n(η_r(A)) = r^{-n}H^n(A): η_r(z) = h(z) − x with h = AffineMap.homothety x r^{-1}, translation by −x is an isometry (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and H^n(h(A)) = |r^{-1}|^n H^n(A) (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Hence H^n⌞η_r(M) = r^{-n}·(η_r)_#(H^n⌞M) as measures: for Borel B, η_r^{-1}(B) is Borel and η_r(η_r^{-1}(B) ∩ M) = B ∩ η_r(M) (Set.image_preimage_inter, η_r bijective), so H^n(B ∩ η_r(M)) = r^{-n}H^n(η_r^{-1}(B) ∩ M). As η_r is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable equivalence, integral_smul_measure and integral_map_equiv give, for every F : ℝ^N → ℝ, ∫_{η_r(M)} F dH^n = r^{-n}∫_M F(η_r(z)) dH^n(z). With F(y) = f(y)θ(x + ry) and x + r·η_r(z) = z:
 (∗) ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x+ry) dH^n(y) = r^{-n}∫_M f(η_r(z))θ(z) dH^n(z).

2. Cutoffs. Fix κ ∈ (0,1). Let f₁(y) := min{1, max{0, (1 − |y|)/(1 − κ)}} and f₂(y) := min{1, max{0, (κ^{-1} − |y|)/(κ^{-1} − 1)}}. They are continuous, [0,1]-valued and vanish outside the compact balls B̄_1(0), resp. B̄_{1/κ}(0), so f₁, f₂ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N,ℝ), and 1_{B̄_κ(0)} ≤ f₁ ≤ 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f₂ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1/κ}(0)}. As |η_r(z)| = |z − x|/r, for every z and r > 0:
 1_{B̄_{κr}(x)}(z) ≤ f₁(η_r z) ≤ 1_{B̄_r(x)}(z) ≤ f₂(η_r z) ≤ 1_{B̄_{r/κ}(x)}(z).

3. Sandwich. Let 0 < r ≤ κr₀ and g_i(z) := f_i(η_r z)θ(z) (i = 1,2). By step 2, g_i vanishes outside B̄_{r/κ}(x) ⊆ B̄_{r₀}(x) and |g_i| ≤ |θ|; f_i∘η_r is continuous and bounded and θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x), so g_i is H^n-integrable on M ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x) and hence (being the indicator of B̄_{r₀}(x) times itself) on M. As M is H^n-null-measurable, H^n⌞M-a.e. point lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀), where g_i ≥ 0 because θ ≥ 0 on M; therefore ∫_M g_i dH^n = J_i(r).toReal with J_i(r) := ∫⁻_M ofReal(f_i(η_r z))·ofReal(θ(z)) dH^n(z) (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Multiplying the inequalities of step 2 by ofReal θ(z) and integrating over M (lintegral_mono; no measurability is needed):
 ν(B̄_{κr}(x)) ≤ J₁(r) ≤ ν(B̄_r(x)) ≤ J₂(r) ≤ ν(B̄_{r/κ}(x)) ≤ ν(B̄_{r₀}(x)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_{r₀}(x)} ofReal θ dH^n < ∞ (Integrable.lintegral_lt_top).
 Put I_i(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f_i(y)θ(x+ry) dH^n(y) and a(r) := r^{-n}·ν(B̄_r(x)).toReal. By (∗), I_i(r) = r^{-n}J_i(r).toReal, so I₁(r) ≤ a(r) ≤ I₂(r) for 0 < r ≤ κr₀.

4. Plane integrals. For s > 0, H^n(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = ω_n s^n: with the restricted inner product P is an n-dimensional inner product space (finrank P = n); the inclusion P → ℝ^N is an isometry mapping the closed s-ball of P onto P ∩ B̄_s(0), so by Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, H^n(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) equals the volume of the closed s-ball of P; a linear isometry equivalence P ≃ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) preserves volume, and the closed s-ball of ℝ^n has volume realUnitBallVolume n·s^n (SimonGMT Chapter01.volume_closedBall_eq_densityNormalization, valid also for n = 0) = ω_n s^n, because realUnitBallVolume n = volume(B̄_1(0)) = volume(B_1(0)) = ω_n (the unit sphere is Lebesgue-null for n ≥ 1, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball; for n = 0 both balls are the whole one-point space). In particular H^n(P ∩ B̄_{1/κ}(0)) < ∞, so f₁, f₂ are H^n⌞P-integrable, and integrating 1_{B̄_κ(0)} ≤ f₁ and f₂ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1/κ}(0)} over P gives
 c₁ := ∫_P f₁ dH^n ≥ ω_nκ^n and c₂ := ∫_P f₂ dH^n ≤ ω_nκ^{-n}.

5. Limits. By the hypothesis applied to f₁ and f₂, I_i(r) → θ(x)c_i as r ↓ 0. By step 3 and θ(x) ≥ 0:
 θ(x)ω_nκ^n ≤ θ(x)c₁ ≤ liminf_{r↓0} a(r) ≤ limsup_{r↓0} a(r) ≤ θ(x)c₂ ≤ θ(x)ω_nκ^{-n}.
 Since κ ∈ (0,1) is arbitrary, a(r) → θ(x)ω_n as r ↓ 0.

6. Conclusion. For 0 < r ≤ r₀, ν(B̄_r(x)) is finite and equals ofReal(a(r)·r^n), so densityRatio n ν x r = ν(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(r)^n) = ofReal(a(r)/ω_n), which tends to ofReal(θ(x)ω_n/ω_n) = ofReal(θ(x)) by continuity of ofReal. Thus HasDensity n ν x (ofReal θ(x)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Change of variables: H^n(η_r(A)) = r^{-n}H^n(A), hence ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x+ry)dH^n = r^{-n}∫_M f(η_r z)θ(z)dH^n.
Continuous compactly supported cutoffs f₁, f₂ with 1_{B̄_κ} ≤ f₁ ≤ 1_{B̄_1} ≤ f₂ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1/κ}}.
For r ≤ κr₀ the weighted integrals are integrable, equal lintegrals, and sandwich r^{-n}ν(B̄_r(x)).
H^n(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = ω_n s^n gives ω_nκ^n ≤ ∫_P f₁ and ∫_P f₂ ≤ ω_nκ^{-n}.
Pass to the limit r↓0 with Definition 1.7, then let κ↑1: r^{-n}ν(B̄_r(x)) → θ(x)ω_n.
Convert to densityRatio: HasDensity n ν x (ofReal θ(x)).

subproblem.title: Upper density theorem: μ⌞A has zero n-density at H^n-a.e. point of U ∖ A (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; parent step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N, U ⊆ ℝ^N open with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and A ⊆ ℝ^N a Borel set. Then for H^n-almost every x ∈ U ∖ A the n-dimensional density of μ⌞A at x exists and equals 0, i.e. (μ⌞A)(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (U A : Set (Euclidean N)), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K ≠ ∞) → MeasurableSet A → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)), x ∈ U → x ∉ A → HasDensity n (μ.restrict A) x 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6, localized as in Remark 3.7(2)). The SimonGMT lemmas used live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison, Chapter01.Densities and Chapter02.AreaLiteral (to be imported by the implementation; they use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n; B̄_s(z) := closedBall z s; for an outer measure ξ on ℝ^N and a set A, Θ*(ξ,A,y) := Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity ξ n A y = limsup_{ρ↓0} ξ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(y))/(realUnitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ)).

1. Countable cover of U by good balls. Fix a countable dense D ⊆ ℝ^N and let F := {(c,q) ∈ D × ℚ : q > 0, B̄_{2q}(c) ⊆ U}, a countable set. For y ∈ U choose ε > 0 with B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U, a rational q ∈ (0, ε/3) and c ∈ D with |c − y| < q; then y ∈ B̄_q(c) and B̄_{2q}(c) ⊆ B̄_{3q}(y) ⊆ U. Hence U ⊆ ⋃_{(c,q)∈F} B̄_q(c).

2. Upper density theorem on one ball. Fix (c,q) ∈ F and let μ_{cq} := μ⌞B̄_{2q}(c); it is a finite measure since B̄_{2q}(c) is a compact subset of U. Its outer measure is Borel regular (Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular); A is Borel, hence Carathéodory measurable for it (MeasureTheory.le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory); and μ_{cq}(A) ≤ μ(B̄_{2q}(c)) < ∞. Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 (real dimension n ≥ 0) yields simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (E_{cq}) = 0 for E_{cq} := {y : y ∉ A ∧ Θ*(μ_{cq},A,y) ≠ 0}. Since simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n = (simonHausdorffMeasureReal n).toOuterMeasure (Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure) and simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = μHE[n] (Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), H^n(E_{cq}) = 0.

3. Identification of the quotients. realUnitBallVolume n = ω_n: by Chapter01.volume_closedBall_eq_densityNormalization with r = 1 the closed unit ball of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) has volume realUnitBallVolume n, and it has the same volume as the open unit ball (Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball for n ≥ 1; for n = 0 both balls are the one-point space). Also ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(ρ)^n (ENNReal.rpow_natCast). Let y ∈ B̄_q(c) and 0 < ρ ≤ q. Then B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B̄_{2q}(c), so μ_{cq}(A ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) = (μ⌞A)(B̄_ρ(y)) (restrict_apply, closed balls being Borel). Hence the quotient defining Θ*(μ_{cq},A,y) equals densityRatio n (μ⌞A) y ρ for all ρ ∈ (0,q], and therefore limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n (μ⌞A) y ρ = Θ*(μ_{cq},A,y) (Filter.limsup_congr).

4. Conclusion. Let y ∈ U with y ∉ A and suppose HasDensity n (μ⌞A) y 0 fails. Choose (c,q) ∈ F with y ∈ B̄_q(c) (step 1). If Θ*(μ_{cq},A,y) = 0, then by step 3 the nonnegative function ρ ↦ densityRatio n (μ⌞A) y ρ has limsup 0 along 𝓝[>]0, hence also liminf 0, so it tends to 0 (tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup) — a contradiction. Thus y ∈ E_{cq}. The exceptional set {y : y ∈ U ∧ y ∉ A ∧ ¬HasDensity n (μ⌞A) y 0} is therefore contained in the countable union ⋃_{(c,q)∈F} E_{cq} of H^n-null sets, so it is H^n-null, which is the asserted a.e. statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many balls B̄_q(c) with B̄_{2q}(c) ⊆ U.
On each ball apply Simon 1.3.6 (Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6) to the finite Borel-regular measure μ⌞B̄_{2q}(c) and the Borel set A; convert Simon's Hausdorff outer measure to μHE[n].
For y ∈ B̄_q(c) and ρ ≤ q, Simon's density quotient equals densityRatio n (μ⌞A) y ρ (same normalization ω_n, ρ^n).
Zero upper density forces the ratio to tend to 0; the exceptional set lies in a countable union of H^n-null sets.

subproblem.title: Weight of v(M,θ) as θH^n⌞M restricted to a Borel hull of the tangent-point set (parent steps 1, 3)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U and M ⊆ ℝ^N, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with V = v(M,θ) (IsVarifoldOf V M θ). Let M* := {x ∈ M : ∃ S ∈ G(N,n) such that M has weighted approximate tangent space S.plane at x with respect to θ (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7)} and ν := (H^n⌞M) with density ofReal∘θ. Then there is a Borel set T ⊇ M* with μ_V = ν⌞T, and μ_V(B) = ∫⁻_{M*∩B} ofReal(θ) dH^n for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), IsVarifoldOf V M θ → ∃ T : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet T ∧ {x | x ∈ M ∧ ∃ S : Grassmannian N n, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane} ⊆ T ∧ V.weight = (((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict M).withDensity fun x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ x)).restrict T ∧ ∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → V.weight B = ∫⁻ x in {x | x ∈ M ∧ ∃ S : Grassmannian N n, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane} ∩ B, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 8 p. 206: V = v(M,θ) means V(A) = μ(π(TM ∩ A)) with μ = H^n⌞θ). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N; G := Grassmannian N n; μ_V := V.weight; HWATS(x,S) := Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane; M* := {x : x ∈ M ∧ ∃ S ∈ G, HWATS(x,S)}; λ := H^n⌞M; ν := λ.withDensity(ofReal∘θ).

1. Unpacking IsVarifoldOf V M θ: M ⊆ U; θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M; θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; and V(A) = ∫⁻ over {x : x ∈ M ∧ ∃ S, HWATS(x,S) ∧ (x,S) ∈ A} of ofReal θ dH^n for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N × G. U is open (V.isOpen_domain).

2. Fourth conjunct. Let B ⊆ ℝ^N be Borel. B × G is Borel and μ_V(B) = V(B × G) (Varifold.weight_apply). For A = B × G, (x,S) ∈ A ⟺ x ∈ B, so {x : x ∈ M ∧ ∃ S, HWATS(x,S) ∧ (x,S) ∈ B × G} = M* ∩ B. By step 1, μ_V(B) = ∫⁻_{M*∩B} ofReal θ dH^n.

3. By the sibling lemma intcpt_id_restrict_sigmaFinite with μ = H^n and U, M, θ as in step 1, λ = H^n⌞M is σ-finite, hence s-finite.

4. First and second conjuncts; hull identity. Let T := toMeasurable λ M*. T is Borel (measurableSet_toMeasurable) and M* ⊆ T (subset_toMeasurable). Since λ is s-finite, λ⌞T = λ⌞M* (Measure.restrict_toMeasurable_of_sFinite). Since M* ⊆ M, λ⌞M* = (H^n⌞M)⌞M* = H^n⌞M* (Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset, valid for arbitrary sets). Hence λ⌞T = H^n⌞M*.

5. Third conjunct. For Borel B: (ν⌞T)(B) = ν(B ∩ T) (restrict_apply) = ∫⁻_{B∩T} ofReal θ dλ (withDensity_apply; B ∩ T is Borel) = ∫⁻ ofReal θ d((λ⌞T)⌞B) (Measure.restrict_restrict for Borel B: (λ⌞T)⌞B = λ⌞(B∩T)) = ∫⁻ ofReal θ d((H^n⌞M*)⌞B) (step 4) = ∫⁻ ofReal θ d(H^n⌞(B∩M*)) (Measure.restrict_restrict) = ∫⁻_{M*∩B} ofReal θ dH^n = μ_V(B) (step 2). Measures agreeing on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext), so μ_V = ν⌞T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsVarifoldOf V M θ and openness of U.
Taking A = B × G and Varifold.weight_apply: μ_V(B) = ∫⁻_{M*∩B} ofReal θ dH^n for Borel B.
H^n⌞M is σ-finite by intcpt_id_restrict_sigmaFinite.
T := toMeasurable (H^n⌞M) M* is Borel, contains M*, and (H^n⌞M)⌞T = (H^n⌞M)⌞M* = H^n⌞M*.
On Borel B, (ν⌞T)(B) = ∫⁻ ofReal θ d((H^n⌞M*)⌞B) = μ_V(B); conclude μ_V = ν⌞T by Measure.ext.
